subject: Supplemental order: scope/pricing rebalance and SOW edits
messages:
From: Maria López <maria.lopez@fathomhealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: contracts@fathomhealth.com
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: supplemental order + pricing rebalance

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is aligned and we'd like to move forward with a supplemental order rather than a full rework of the existing MSA. Goal: add 2000 reserved inference hours over a 6-month phased ramp, but we also need to rebalance our existing credits (shift ~30% from evaluation tier to production).

Couple of asks up front:
- We need a revised order form showing the phased capacity add and a new blended unit price for the added capacity.
- Can you confirm whether the current data retention / audit-log language in the MSA will apply to the new capacity, or if we should sign an amendment to call that out? (Our compliance team is asking explicitly.)
- Would Redwood accept an initial 60-day top-up commitment with a midpoint reassessment (instead of annual comm)?

I've attached a simple supplemental order template so you can see our expected structure.

Thanks,
Maria
Contracts | Fathom Health

---

On Wed, 05 Aug 2026 at 14:35, sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com wrote:
From: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: Maria López <maria.lopez@fathomhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: supplemental order + pricing rebalance

Hi Maria — appreciate the clear asks and the template. Looping in Karthik (sales) and Laura (legal).

Quick responses:
- We can do a phased 6-month top-up with a 60-day initial commitment and a formal reassessment at the 60-day mark. I will propose two billing profiles (monthly amortized vs. up-front credit purchase) so your finance team has options.
- Data retention / audit logs: Laura, can you confirm whether the existing MSA language covers additional reserved capacity or if we should draft a short amendment that references the same retention schedule?
- I'll draft a supplemental order that shows the blended unit price for the added capacity and the movement of credits between tiers; expect a redline back by EOD Friday.

Next steps: I will prepare the redline supplemental order and a brief summary memo for your compliance team calling out the data-retention applicability. If there are specific retention windows Fathom requires, please send them so Laura can confirm.

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---

On Fri, 07 Aug 2026 at 09:05, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com wrote:
From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: supplemental order + pricing rebalance

Sergio / Karthik — I reviewed the template Maria sent. High-level legal notes: 
- The existing MSA Section 4.2 (Data Retention and Logs) is written to cover all services provided under active orders; an amendment is not strictly necessary if you simply attach the supplemental order as an addendum referencing the master agreement. That said, the compliance team wants the retention window explicitly called out in the cover memo (they often require a contractual cross-reference).
- Pricing/credits: no legal blockers. We should avoid language that creates a new "service" definition — call it "Supplemental Reserved Capacity" and reference the applicable SKU in the order form.
- Procurement asked that we include a change-control clause in the supplemental order describing the process for rebalancing credits mid-term (notice period, approval path). I drafted suggested language below.

Suggested change-control snippet (to include in the supplemental order):
"Any reallocation of previously purchased credits between evaluation and production tiers requires 30 days' written notice and mutual approval by authorized procurement contacts. Such reallocations will be processed on the next billing cycle and are subject to the pricing bands outlined in Exhibit A. No retrospective refunds will be provided for previously consumed credits."

I'll prepare a redline of the supplemental order and include the short memo for Fathom's compliance team. If Fathom wants a 60-day commitment with a midpoint reassessment, operationally that's doable; we should capture how the reassessment will affect the billing profile.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

---

Sergio — thanks for the quick loop-in. A couple clarifications from our side after a procurement review: 
- The compliance team wants the audit-log SLA to be explicitly restated (they asked for a 24-month retention minimum). Can you confirm that Redwood can commit to 24 months for logs tied to this supplemental capacity?
- On pricing: Fathom is willing to accept a blended unit rate for the added capacity if Redwood will include a 2% monthly price protection (cap) during the 6-month phased ramp. That keeps our finance planning stable while you scale.

We'd like to get a redline back by Friday so procurement can start approvals.

Regards,
Maria

Maria — attaching our redline and the short compliance memo. Summary of what we captured: 
- Redwood has accepted the 24-month audit-log retention for logs associated with the supplemental reserved capacity. The retention commitment is added as a short exhibit referencing Section 4.2 of the MSA.
- We created a "Supplemental Reserved Capacity" order form that:
  - Adds 2000 reserved inference hours phased over 6 months (500/mo ramp),
  - Shows the credit reallocation movement (30% from evaluation to production) with a clear account of remaining credits,
  - Applies a blended unit price for the added capacity and includes the 2% monthly price protection cap during the 6-month ramp.
- Included the suggested change-control clause from legal (30 days' notice, approval path, billing timing).

Attachments: Redwood_redline_Supplement_v2.docx (redline of the order form), Supplemental_Order_Summary_for_Compliance.pdf (short memo)

Next steps: Maria, once you confirm the redline, Laura will prepare a clean exhibit for signature and Karthik will follow up on billing options. If procurement wants any minor tweaks to the wording on change-control, we can incorporate them in a single pass.

Thanks —
Sergio
